transcript:
Header: 2025-10-07 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Reed (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - NovaHealth), Priya Raman (Lead Engineer), Evan Torres (ML Engineer)

Summary: Quick review of last week's integration, results from initial runs, discussion on SDK function/tool-calling behavior and structured output validation, and next steps to finalize pilot success criteria and run deeper benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I think we're at our weekly sync for NovaHealth POC, hope the time still works.
[00:08] Marcus: yep all good, thanks. want to go through the results you sent and a few integration questions.
[00:14] Jordan: great. Samira, do you want to kick us off with the SDK changes we pushed last week?
[00:19] Samira: sure. so we published a small SDK patch that adds clearer function-calling helpers and a structured-output validator. the sample repo has two flows: one is a direct function-call where the model returns the function name + args, the other is tool-augmented where the model invokes a retriever tool. both flows support streaming responses and non-streaming.
[00:38] Priya: quick question — in your sample, is the validation strict? we need to reject malformed outputs server-side rather than rely on client parsing.
[00:46] Samira: yes the validator can run either client-side or in our middleware. by default the SDK validates against a JSON-schema you pass. we also added a "best-effort repair" flag where Redwood will try to coerce types or request model to re-emit if schema doesn't match — it's an opt-in because it can add latency.
[01:05] Evan: did you test nested function arguments? our tools sometimes return nested JSON objects for patient metadata and the earlier function flow flattened those, which broke our ingestion.
[01:14] Samira: good point. we added recursive parsing and an option to preserve opaque blobs as base64. but we saw a couple of edge cases where ASR/transcription style errors made key names slightly off, so you may want to add canonical key mapping.
[01:30] Marcus: when you say "function-call" is that the same as the Redwood "tool calling" we saw in the deck? I got confused between product names earlier.
[01:36] Jordan: yeah sorry — terminology gets fuzzy. function-calling in the SDK is our wrapper for tool calls; same concept, just different surface. sometimes internal docs say "tool calls", SDK docs say "function calls".
[01:45] Marcus: ok that clarifies.
[01:48] Samira: we also measured latency and success-rate for the two flows. for the NovaHealth sample workload (avg prompt length ~120 tokens, response ~220 tokens) hosted API median latency for non-streaming function flow was ~420ms per request, streaming start-of-response around 180ms and full response ~700ms. success-rate (first-pass schema-valid returns) was ~88% for streaming + validator disabled, and ~81% with strict validation enabled — the repair flow bumped it to ~94% but added ~120ms on average.
[02:22] Priya: that's helpful. what's the token cost delta for the repair flow? we need to track cost closely.
[02:27] Samira: approximate extra tokens per failed validation was about 30-40 tokens (re-emit prompt + system instruction). across your sample dataset it added ~6% token overhead.
[02:36] Evan: on the dedicated side, if we switch to Redwood Dedicated, do you have numbers on throughput with batching? we saw some docs but wanted concrete numbers for our concurrency pattern.
[02:46] Samira: yes. on dedicated with a 4-GPU pool and continuous batching enabled, we achieved ~800 reqs/min for your average size with 100ms median latency at 95th perc for the batched path. caveat: batching depends on arrival patterns; we can set max delay to prioritize latency.
[03:06] Marcus: that 95th percentile 100ms sounds great, but is that end-to-end or token-generation time?
[03:12] Samira: that's token-generation median; end-to-end including our network hop to your VPC adds about 30-60ms depending on region.
[03:20] Jordan: quick interjection — during last week's run we also noticed a few errors related to KMS-integrated keys when storing KV cache metadata in the private agent. Samira, you had a remediation note?
[03:29] Samira: yes, for Private deployments the KV cache metadata should be encrypted with the instance-local KMS alias. we pushed a config change that avoids double-encrypting — that was causing decrypt failures during warm cache lookups.
[03:41] Priya: great. another integration question — how do we handle retries for function calls if the tool endpoint fails? we don't want duplicate side-effects.
[03:49] Samira: recommended pattern: use idempotency keys and give the tool a retry-safe interface (e.g., upsert semantics). the SDK automatically attaches a request-id and you can enable semantic dedupe on the tool connector. if your tool cannot be made idempotent, we recommend an async invocation path and a confirm/commit model.
[04:08] Evan: we also observed occasional hallucinations where the model invented a nonexistent patient lookup ID and then the tool returned 404. any tips?
[04:16] Samira: couple tactics: tighten system prompts to forbid fabrications and prefer retrieval-augmented generation; add a verification step where the tool returns a signature that the model must include when calling back, and enforce via schema. also lower temperature and use logit bias to discourage certain tokens — all available in the SDK config.
[04:37] Marcus: on compliance — we need audit logs and SSO mapping for user actions in the console. last week you said Redwood Console supports token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing — does that integrate with our SIEM?
[04:48] Jordan: yes, Console can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure webhook or forwarder; for Private we can write to your S3 with KMS encryption for retention. we also support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[04:58] Priya: can we get the SOC2 docs and network diagram? security asked for it.
[05:03] Jordan: I'll attach the SOC2 and the architecture diagram to the follow-up email.
[05:07] Samira: back to the SDK — Evan mentioned nested JSON edge-case. if the model returns slightly different key names (e.g., patient_id vs patientId), the validator can map via a configurable synonyms list. we can include an example mapping in the sample repo.
[05:23] Priya: perfect. also, for structured output, do you support partial streaming of JSON objects? our UI renders incremental fields as they come in.
[05:33] Samira: yes, we support streaming of structured chunks. the SDK emits partial objects with a continuation token; the validator can accept partials and then run final validation on close. that's what improved time-to-first-field in our streaming tests.
[05:47] Marcus: for the next benchmark can you include one run with streaming partials and one with non-streaming so we can compare perceived latency in the UI?
[05:54] Samira: yes will include.
[05:56] Evan: a small bug we noticed — when using structured output + function-calling, if the model returns a function name but the args are empty, the SDK tried to call the tool with null and that caused a server error.
[06:07] Samira: thanks — we already added guard logic to skip tool invocation if args are empty and surface a structured error back to the app. that fix is in the patch I published.
[06:16] Jordan: moving to metrics — Marcus, do you have the pass/fail numbers from your internal runs?
[06:21] Marcus: yes. out of 1200 flows run against our sample dataset, strict schema first-pass success was 78%, with 17% repaired by the best-effort flow, and 5% failed and required manual review. average host cost was inline with what you estimated, but we saw some outliers up to 3x during peak concurrency.
[06:39] Jordan: those peaks are usually due to token length variance and retries. Samira, any suggestions to flatten that?
[06:44] Samira: set an informed max_tokens based on prompt distribution, implement prefix/caching for repeated context (we saw 30-40% savings with KV caching for NovaHealth prompts), and consider quantized model variants for non-sensitive workloads.
[06:57] Evan: about quantization — are there any known quality regressions for our tasks if we go 4-bit?
[07:03] Samira: depends on the model. we have per-model quantization profiles. for the LLM family you prototyped, 4-bit had negligible regressions on extraction tasks but showed slight drop on generative tone — we'd recommend A/B testing in the POC.
[07:18] Priya: timeline question — we are aiming to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted by Oct 24. what do you need from us?
[07:25] Jordan: final success criteria, your GA compliance checklist, and a couple of production prompt sets. once we run the dedicated benchmark and network deep dive, we can give a concrete commit recommendation.
[07:34] Marcus: ok we'll try to get those to you by Oct 13.
[07:37] Samira: quick note on monitoring — Console provides per-route latency and token breakdown. we'll add a sample dashboard for your key routes and seed alerts for failures and schema-rejection rates.
[07:48] Evan: can the alerting be exported to PagerDuty?
[07:51] Jordan: yes, webhook or native PD integration.
[07:54] Priya: two final minor items — one, do you have a sample terraform module for provisioning a Private deployment agent? two, what's the onboarding for our security folks to run penetration/security review?
[08:04] Samira: we have a terraform module in the repo; Jordan will link it. for security review we can set up a read-only cross-account role and provide network diagrams, SOC2, pen-test history, and a temporary test instance.
[08:18] Jordan: OK let's recap next steps. we'll send the docs (integration guide, SOC2, terraform sample), Samira will run the three benchmark variants (hosted streaming structured partials, hosted non-streaming, dedicated batched), NovaHealth to provide prompt sets and success criteria. plan deep dive for private infra week of Oct 20.
[08:36] Marcus: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:38] Jordan: thanks, talk soon.

Questions noted: What is the expected first-pass schema success threshold for production? (Customer to define) How to handle non-idempotent tool side-effects? (Use idempotency or async confirm flows)

References shared: sample repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/novahealth-poc (sent in chat) ; benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in meeting notes) ; SOC2 summary (to be attached)

End of transcript.
